subject: br-codigo-penal
citation: Decreto-Lei nº 2.848, de 7 de dezembro de 1940 — Código Penal (Brazil), as compiled by the Presidência da República (Planalto), current through Lei nº 15.517 de 2026; DOU 31.12.1940, retificado 3.1.1941; LexML urn:lex:br:federal:decreto.lei:1940-12-07;2848
note: Fetched by the conducting session (P1 is the conductor's, not an encoder's). LexML is the index; it names Planalto's 'Texto Atualizado Multivigente' as the updated text, the Câmara and Senado copies as the ORIGINAL 1940 publication. Planalto's compilation is not the official text — only the Diário Oficial is, and the page itself says so — but it is the consolidation Brazilian practice reads, and it is the only one LexML offers as updated. The raw HTML is not byte-reproducible. The HTML bytes change on every request: Planalto's F5 load balancer injects a per-request telemetry <script id="f5_cspm"> near the end of the page. Two fetches on 2026-09-29 (sha256 bfc589f8… and 9c564ca9…) differ only there. The digest above pins the copy held at source/del2848compilado.htm; a re-fetch will not reproduce it. The law text is pinned by the assembled artifact's digest, which both fetches reproduced byte for byte. Encoders read source/codigo-penal-1940.txt and nothing else. retrieval_cost counts the two TIMED requests of fetch.sh's first version (LexML record and compilado). The Senado record, the licence check against Lei 9.610 and the normas.leg.br probes were fetched afterwards and not timed, so they are absent from it rather than estimated.
in_force_absent_reason: Planalto's compiled page carries no currency banner of the 'up to date as of' kind. Its only statement about itself is the footer 'Este texto não substitui o publicado no DOU de 31.12.1940 e retificado em 3.1.1941', which disclaims authority rather than stating currency. The latest amending instrument cited inline is Lei nº 15.517, de 2026 (20 citations), so currency is inferred to be no earlier than that law — an inference, not a publisher's statement, which is why it is not recorded as in_force.

assembled.note: UTF-8 plain text, one source paragraph per line, produced by source/extract.py from the Planalto HTML, decoded as Windows-1252. (The first extraction decoded it as ISO-8859-1, which turned 80 en dashes and one closing quote into invisible C1 control characters; an independent test author found it the same day, and the corrected extraction differs on exactly those 81 lines and those characters.) The output is also Unicode-normalised to NFC: two lines, art. 121-A § 2º and art. 339, arrive with decomposed accents, found by two test authors the same day. Six <strike> spans (revoked matter under arts. 187-196) are wrapped ⟦STRUCK: …⟧ so they cannot be read as current law. Amendment and 'Vide' notes are kept inline. This is the file P3 encodes from and every quotation is copied from.

documents.title: Código Penal — Decreto-Lei nº 2.848/1940, texto compilado (Presidência da República, Casa Civil)
documents.citation: Decreto-Lei nº 2.848, de 7 de dezembro de 1940 (Código Penal), texto compilado
documents.covers_absent_reason: A compiled text states the law as currently amended, not a dated range. The earliest date it could state is the last amending law cited inline (Lei nº 15.517, de 2026), whose own publication and vigência dates were not retrieved in P1; P2's prospective sweep is where that is settled.

annotations.inventory_note: Every '(Vide …)' pointer in the compiled text, numbered V1–V33 in source order, plus V34–V38; source/vide-index.tsv maps each marker to its line in source/codigo-penal-1940.txt and the instrument it points at. These are Planalto's cross-references to OTHER instruments and to constitutional rulings of the STF (ADPF 54, 779, 569, 881, 1107, 1207; ADI 7032) — exactly the external modifications P2 must dispose of one by one, which is why this inventory is declared complete. V34–V38 are five BARE pointers ('Vide Lei nº 8.072, de 25.7.90', no parentheses, source lines 1190–1201, arts. 158–159) that the first inventory missed because it matched only '(Vide …)'. Sweep-b found them. They were appended rather than interleaved so that the ids already cited by the three sweep registers stay valid. Measured after the correction: 38 occurrences of the word 'Vide' in the text, 33 parenthesised and 5 bare, and all 38 are inventoried.

1131 inline notes of the form '(Redação dada pela Lei …)', '(Incluído pela Lei …)', '(Revogado pela Lei …)'. Not enumerated as individual markers: each records an amendment that the compilation has ALREADY applied to the text, so the text is the disposition. P2 disposes of the class, and of any single note whose amendment is prospective (see the vigencia scheme).

74 '(Vigência)' links, each pointing at the vigência clause of the amending law. Not enumerated: most are historical. A link attached to a 2025-2026 amendment may mark text not yet in force, and P2's prospective sweep must check every amending law of 2025-2026 for vacatio legis rather than trust this class.
